{{nihongo|'''Izusahime Shrine'''|伊豆佐比売神社}} is a [[shinto shrine]] in the [[Engishiki Jinmyōchō]]. It is located in [[Mutsu Province]].

It is said to be a god listed in the Engishiki Shinmyocho. Q1996}}) During the annual festival on April 15th, I heard from the representative of the shrine parishioners that it is also called ``Izu Samo''.</ref>) It is said to be enshrined as the god of good harvest.

"Engishiki Nairiku Oku 100-za Heisei Pilgrimage Record"<ref name="hyakuza">Kenma Honda "Engishiki Nairiku Oku 100-za Heisei Pilgrimage Record" Shrine Shimpo Project June 1997. </ref> states that it is unclear what kind of god Izu Sahime no Mikoto is, according to research in the ``Dainippon Shinto Name Dictionary'' <ref> Edited by Yoshihiko Umeda, ``Dainippon Shinto Name Dictionary'', Hori Shoten, December 1972</ref>, and offers two theories regarding the deity enshrined at this shrine.
#``God of hot water'' theory:{{ill|Deguchi Nobutsune|ja|出口延経|qid=Q108780926}}'s "{{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō Studies|ja|神名帳考証|qid=Q11588824}}" volume 5<ref name="koushou">"Shinmeicho kosho" is edited by Yoshi Saeki, "Jingi Zensho Volume 1", Koten Kokyukyo Included in October 1906. </ref> states, ``{{ill|Izu Province|Q860928|qid=Q860928}}Izu Nabi Mikoto Shrine, Ankokurei, {{ill|Dewa Province|Q876032|qid=Q876032}}{{ill|Yuzusame Shrine|Q11577650|qid=Q11577650|lt=Yuzume Samo Shrine}}.'' Yuzusa of Yuzusamo Shrine means ``Yudezawa'' and is said to be the guardian deity of hot springs<ref>In the Engishiki Nairiku 100-za Heisei Pilgrimage Record, the enshrined deity of Yuzusamo Shrine is Mizohime no Mikoto, who is also worshiped as the god of hot springs in various places. k|Ōkuninushi|Q276944|Omiki}} and {{ill|Sukunabikona|Q3275687|qid=Q3275687|lt=Sukohikona}} are also enshrined, so it may not be possible to conclude that Mizohime no Mikoto is the god of hot springs alone. </ref>. Furthermore, from "Rifu Town History"<ref name="choushi">, edited by Rifu Town History Compilation Committee, "Rifu Town History", Rifu Town History Compilation Committee, March 1986. </ref> "Yumusahime Shrine in Tagawa District, Dewa Province (currently {{ill|Yamagata Prefecture|Q125863|qid=Q125863}}{{ill|Tsuruoka|Q734416|qid=Q734416}} Yutagawa)" The same deity was enshrined, and the springing of hot springs was probably considered a divine act, and the goddess was the god who created things.I wonder if there was hot springs in Sawaoto or Unohara at that time. Today, there are two hot springs still flowing within 4km of this shrine, and one of these, ``Sawaoto-no-Yu,'' is located in the Enoki River basin, and the ``Rokuta Ruins'', the remains of early Jomon settlements, are located on the hills leading from the shrine to the Enoki River.{{ill|Shōwa era|ar|فترة شووا|br|Oadvezh Shōwa|ca|Període Shōwa|cs|Období Šówa|de|Shōwa-Zeit|eo|Ŝova-epoko|es|Era Shōwa|eu|Shōwa aroa|fa|دوره شووا|fi|Shōwa-kausi|fr|Ère Shōwa (1926-1989)|he|תקופת שווה|hi|शोवा युग|hu|Sóva-kor|id|Zaman Shōwa|it|Periodo Shōwa|ja|昭和|ka|შოვას პერიოდი|ko|쇼와 시대|lt|Šiova laikotarpis|ms|Zaman Shōwa|nl|Showaperiode|no|Shōwa-perioden|pl|Shōwa|pt|Período Shōwa|ru|Сёва|simple|Shōwa era|sr|Шова период|sv|Shōwa|th|ยุคโชวะ|tl|Panahong Shōwa|tr|Şova Dönemi|uk|Період Сьова|vi|Thời kỳ Chiêu Hòa|zh|昭和|zh_classical|昭和|zh_min_nan|Chiau-hô|zh_yue|昭和|qid=Q327567}}The excavation in 1985|Q2431}} seems to be unrelated to the development of this land and the construction of this shrine.#“God of grain spirits” theory
:The enshrinement site ``Iidoi'' is said to be an accent of ``Iitoyo'' by Kaoru Hongo, author of ``Dewa Mutsu no Kosha'' in his book, and he makes the following inference. In other words, among the 100 {{ill|Mutsu Province|ca|Província de Mutsu|cs|Provincie Mucu|de|Provinz Mutsu|es|Provincia de Mutsu|fa|ولایت موتسو|fi|Mutsun provinssi|fr|Province de Mutsu|gl|Provincia de Mutsu|id|Provinsi Mutsu|it|Mutsu (provincia)|ja|陸奥国|ko|무쓰국|lt|Mucu žemė|nl|Mutsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Mutsu|ru|Муцу (провинция)|simple|Mutsu Province|sk|Mucu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Муцу|tr|Mutsu (vilayet)|uk|Муцу (провінція)|zh|陸奧國|zh_classical|陸奧國|zh_min_nan|Mutu-kok|zh_yue|陸奧國|qid=Q907389}} shrines listed in the ``Engishiki Shinmecho,'' the god where hot springs gush out is called the ``Onsen Shrine,'' and the shrines associated with ``Iitoyo'' are said to be ``the god of granaries'' and ``the god of production,'' rather than the ``god of hot springs.'' Also, ``Shinmeicho Kosho Volume 5'' <ref name="koushou" In the entry for this shrine in In ``Shako'' and ``Shinmeicho Koshi Volume 5'', the deity enshrined at this shrine is {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyoukehime}}, the god of grain spirits. "Mutsu Shiki Shako" is owned by the Suifu Meitokukai and Shokokan Bunko. </ref>I introduced this and considered that it would not be unnatural to enshrine the god of grain spirits, considering the topography of the enshrined place and the reason why the wealthy farmer {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumonchoja}} was established.Also, in the "Engishiki Nairiku Oku 100 Za Heisei Pilgrimage Record" <ref name="hyakuza" />, "Ou Kanseimon Roshi" written in {{ill|Kyōhō|Q1145048|qid=Q1145048}}4 ({{ill|1719|Q6902|qid=Q6902}}) <ref name="monroushi">Yoshikazu Sakuma From “Ou Kansekimon Roshi” edited by Hobundo Publishing, October 1972. </ref> mentions that the enshrined deity is Kausahime, whose furigana in ``Hunai Fudoki'' is ``Mizokuihime''</ref>, and the same book does not include any special description of Mizokui Hime, but only says ``Keida 28 bundles Sanke Tadokoro Festival Mizokui Himeya.'' Furthermore, from "Hunai Fudoki Volume 4" in the first year of {{ill|An'ei|Q1193910|qid=Q1193910|lt=Yasunaga}} ({{ill|1772|Q7690|qid=Q7690}}) <ref> "Hunai Fudoki" edited by Nozomi Tanabe, published by Hobundo Publishing, November 1975. </ref>, etc., have errors in the exact same part regarding the addition of this shrine. The article dated August 7, 2007 ({{ill|852|Q30383|qid=Q30383}}) states that he is ``Kasho 5th rank, lower rank,'' but in ``Ou Kanseimon Roshi'' and ``Hunai Fudoki,'' it is written in July 2017 as ``Jishō 5th lower rank.'' </ref>From this, it is speculated that various magazines written afterward, such as ``Hunai Fudoki,'' were written based on ``Ou Kansekimon Roshi.''Based on these, “Engishiki Nairiku Oku 100 Za Heisei Pilgrimage Record”<ref name="hyakuza" So, if we consider the enshrined deity to be ``Izu Sahime no Mikoto'', ``Izu'' is strict, ``Sa'' has the prefix meaning of promoting something, and ``Hime'' is a woman who is believed to be the root of production, so it can be thought of as ``the god of generation, growth, growth,'' that is, the ``god of the spirit of grain and guardian of Kuramasa'' who protects local production. From the "Miyagi Prefecture Shrine Directory" <ref name="meikan">, edited by the Miyagi Prefectural Shrine Agency, which lists the enshrined deity as Mizokui Himen-no-Mikoto, "Miyagi Prefecture Shrine Directory", Miyagi Prefecture Shrine Agency, October 1976. </ref> has written at the end of the section for this shrine, ``The {{ill|Engishiki Jinmyōchō|Q11064932|qid=Q11064932|lt=Shiki}} says Izu Samo Shrine, and the {{ill|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|cs|Nihon Montoku Tennó Džicuroku|de|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|es|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|ff|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|fr|Nihon Montoku tennō jitsuroku|ja|日本文徳天皇実録|ko|일본문덕천황실록|pt|Nihon Montoku Tennō Jitsuroku|zh|日本文德天皇實錄|qid=Q1052905|lt=Buntoku Jitsuroku}} is made for Izu Sama Shrine.How about making it the shrine transmission Mizokuihiba...''. From "Rifu Village Journal" <ref name="sonshi"> Edited by Rifu Village Village Journal Editorial Committee, "Rifu Village History", Rifu Village Office, March 1963. </ref> says, ``This shrine is a female, primarily in charge of water irrigation in the rice-growing area, and the shrine has been revered day and night throughout the area since ancient times, since the paddy fields were cultivated.'' Based on what is written here, it is considered that the deity of this shrine is either Izu Sahime no Mikoto or {{ill|Toyouke-hime|Q2983724|qid=Q2983724|lt=Toyoukehime no Mikoto}}, who is the ``goddess of a bountiful harvest.''Another different theory is “Engishiki Nairiku Oku 100 Za Heisei Pilgrimage Record”<ref name="hyakuza" />In the 7th year of An'ei ({{ill|1778|Q7713|qid=Q7713}}), the ``Engishiki Mutsu 100 Za worship records'' states, ``Itsu Sahime no Mikoto-no-seki, the commoner Akutama Gozen toun.'' (Akutama Gozen For details, see {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Kumonchoja-yashiki Ruins}} below), but it also states that it seems inappropriate to connect Akutama Gozen with the deity enshrined at this shrine.

In any case, both the chief priest and parishioners currently enshrine the deity of this shrine as Izu Sahime no Mikoto, the god of bountiful harvests.

=== History ===The year of its establishment is unknown, but it is written in "Ou Kansekimon Roshi" <ref name="monroushi" "{{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hounai Meisekishi}}" written in the first year of {{ill|Kanpō|Q1145798|qid=Q1145798}} ({{ill|1741|Q7573|qid=Q7573}}), {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Shinsen Mutsu Fudoki}} written in the first year of {{ill|Man'en|Q1193862|qid=Q1193862}} ({{ill|1860|Q7691|qid=Q7691}}) <ref name="sinsen">Mitsunori Yasuda, "Shinsen Mutsu Fudoki", Rekishi Toshosha, November 1980. According to </ref>, in {{ill|Emperor Tenmu|Q335181|qid=Q335181}}2 ({{ill|unofficial era name|Q11248480|qid=Q11248480}}, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Hakuho}}2, {{ill|673|ab|673|af|673|als|673|am|673 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|673|ar|673|ary|673|ast|673|az|673|azb|۶۷۳ (میلادی)|be|673|be_x_old|673|bg|673|bn|৬৭৩|bpy|মারি ৬৭৩|br|673|bs|673.|ca|673|cdo|673 nièng|ceb|673|ckb|٦٧٣|crh|673|cs|673|cv|673|cy|673|da|673|de|673|el|673|eml|673|eo|673|es|673|et|673|eu|673|fa|۶۷۳ (میلادی)|fi|673|fo|673|fr|673|frr|673|fy|673|ga|673|gan|673年|gd|673|gl|673|he|673|hi|673|hr|673.|ht|673 (almanak jilyen)|hu|673|hy|673|id|673|io|673|it|673|ja|673年|jv|673|ka|673|kk|673 жыл|ko|673년|la|673|lb|673|lij|673|lmo|673|lt|673 m.|map_bms|673|mdf|673|mg|673|mhr|673|mk|673|mr|इ.स. ६७३|mrj|673 и|ms|673|mzn|۶۷۳|nah|673|nap|673|nds|673|nds_nl|673|new|सन् ६७३|nl|673|nn|673|no|673|nrm|673|nso|673|oc|673|or|୬୭୩|os|673-æм аз|pl|673|pnb|673|pt|673|qu|673|ro|673|ru|673 год|rue|673|sa|६७३|scn|673|sd|673ع|se|673|sh|673.|shn|673|si|673|sk|673|sl|673|sq|673|sr|673|su|673|sv|673|sw|673|tg|Соли 673|th|พ.ศ. 1216|tk|673|tl|673|tly|673|tr|673|tt|673 ел|uk|673|ur|673ء|uz|673|vec|673|vi|673|war|673|wuu|673年|xmf|673|zh|673年|zh_min_nan|673 nî|zh_yue|673年|qid=Q31105}}), he is said to have held a divine festival by dedicating Keida (a rice field given by the god of heaven for rituals), and in ``Hunai Meisekishi'' it is further written as ``an ancient shrine.'' == Company name ==
The name registered with the Miyagi Prefectural Shrine Agency is ``Izu Sahime Shrine.''

It is sometimes written as ``Izusahime Shrine'' or ``Izu Satsuhime Shrine,'' but the plaque inside the worship hall and the ``Engishiki Shinmyocho'' are written as ``Izusame Shrine.'' In "Engishiki Nairiku Oku 100 Za, Heisei Pilgrimage Record" <ref name="hyakuza" />, it is written in "Japanese Emperor Montoku Annals" as {{ill|Mutsu Province|ca|Província de Mutsu|cs|Provincie Mucu|de|Provinz Mutsu|es|Provincia de Mutsu|fa|ولایت موتسو|fi|Mutsun provinssi|fr|Province de Mutsu|gl|Provincia de Mutsu|id|Provinsi Mutsu|it|Mutsu (provincia)|ja|陸奥国|ko|무쓰국|lt|Mucu žemė|nl|Mutsu (provincie)|pt|Província de Mutsu|ru|Муцу (провинция)|simple|Mutsu Province|sk|Mucu (provincia)|sr|Провинција Муцу|tr|Mutsu (vilayet)|uk|Муцу (провінція)|zh|陸奧國|zh_classical|陸奧國|zh_min_nan|Mutu-kok|zh_yue|陸奧國|qid=Q907389}}'''Izusama-jin'', and this ``''''' is definitely ``''me''', so it is considered that ``Izusame Shrine'' is correct.

Also, in the "Shinsen Mutsu Fudoki" <ref name="sinsen" />, it is written that "local people call it '''the palace of the princess''', but in the "Engishiki Nairiku Oku 100 Theaters Heisei Pilgrimage Record" <ref name="hyakuza" According to the author's interview in the 1990s, only people over the age of 80 called it ``Ohime no Miya,'' and other people called it ``Izusahime Shrine.''

== Cultural properties/remains ==
*<span id="Ruins of Kumonchoja residence">'''Ruins of Kumonchoja residence'''</span>
It is said that the hill on which this shrine is located was once the residence of a famous person in Oshu called ``Kumonchoja'', and the following legend remains.
:Among the servants of the ruler is the princess of Itsuki Dainagon, a {{ill|Kuge|ar|كوجي (منصب)|ca|Kuge|cs|Kuge|de|Kuge (Adel)|es|Kuge|fa|کوگه|fr|Kuge|it|Kuge|ja|公家|ko|공가|ms|Kuge|pl|Kuge|pt|Kuge|ru|Кугэ|sv|Kuge|ta|குகே|th|คูเงะ|tr|Kuge|uk|Куґе|vi|Kuge|zh|公家|qid=Q1196276}} of {{ill|Kii Province|Q864053|qid=Q864053|lt=Kii}}. ink|Ise Grand Shrine|Q687168|Ise} There was a woman named {{ill|Akudama|ja|悪玉姫|qid=Q85880359|lt=Akudama}} who was kidnapped on her way home from a pilgrimage and sold as a servant to a wealthy man. She prayed to her guardian deity, {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Avalokitesvara}}, to make her appear as an ugly woman to ordinary people, but to people of high status as the beautiful princess she was. , usually had a very ugly appearance, but on the occasion of the {{ill|UNKNOWN|lt=Ezo Conquest}}, he stopped by the house of a wealthy man.{{ill|Sakanoue Tamuramaro|ja|坂上田村丸|qid=Q85878315|lt=Sakanoue Tamuramaro}}, she gave birth to a son on August 1, {{ill|Enryaku|de|Enryaku|es|Enryaku|fa|انریاکو|fr|Ère Enryaku|ia|Enryaku|id|Enryaku|it|Enryaku|ja|延暦|ko|엔랴쿠|pt|Enryaku|ru|Энряку (нэнго)|simple|Enryaku|sr|Енрјаку|tr|Enryaku|uk|Енряку (ненґо)|zh|延曆|zh_yue|延曆|qid=Q1373176}}18 ({{ill|799|ab|799|af|799|am|799 እ.ኤ.አ.|an|799|ar|799|ary|799|ast|799|az|799|azb|۷۹۹ (میلادی)|bcl|799|be|799|be_x_old|799|bg|799|bn|৭৯৯|bpy|মারি ৭৯৯|br|799|bs|799.|ca|799|cdo|799 nièng|ceb|799|ckb|٧٩٩|crh|799|cs|799|cv|799 çул|cy|799|da|799|de|799|el|799|eml|799|eo|799|es|799|et|799|eu|799|fa|۷۹۹ (میلادی)|fi|799|fo|799|fr|799|fy|799|ga|799|gan|799年|gd|799|gl|799|he|799|hi|799|hr|799.|ht|799 (almanak jilyen)|hu|799|hy|799|id|799|io|799|is|799|it|799|ja|799年|jv|799|ka|799|kaa|799|kk|799 жыл|ko|799년|la|799|lb|799|lij|799|lmo|799|lt|799 m.|lv|799. gads|map_bms|799|mdf|799|mg|799|mhr|799|mk|799|mr|इ.स. ७९९|mrj|799 и|ms|799|mzn|۷۹۹|nah|799|nap|799|nds|799|new|सन् ७९९|nl|799|nn|799|no|799|nrm|799|nso|799|oc|799|or|୭୯୯|os|799-æм аз|pl|799|pnb|799|pt|799|qu|799|ro|799|ru|799 год|rue|799|sa|७९९|scn|799|sd|799ع|sh|799.|shn|799|si|799|sk|799|sl|799|sq|799|sr|799|su|799|sv|799|sw|799|tg|Соли 799|th|พ.ศ. 1342|tk|799|tl|799|tly|799|tr|799|tt|799 ел|uk|799|ur|799ء|uz|799|vec|799|vi|799|war|799|wuu|799年|xmf|799|zh|799年|zh_min_nan|799 nî|zh_yue|799年|qid=Q33488}}), and gave birth to this child as Chikuma. He was named Senkumamaru, and when Chikumamaru turned 13, they went to Tokyo together and met Tamuramaro, and Chikumamaru became the second Tamuramaro, according to a local information board. (The signboard near the center of the image of ``Kumonchoja Residence Ruins.'')</ref>.

worked on it, and even to the person who bought the wood, so it is said that the buyer delivered the slices to a shrine and held a festival. In addition, the grain of the wood was beautiful, even down to the branches, so people from the area took it home, but they were horrified because it was believed that some disaster had happened, so they returned it and it is said that it is piled up under a rain cover.
